definitions_implemented.T: CLOCK_MONOTONIC (time.monotonic_ns) from just before the sandboxed Driver is spawned to the caller's oracle-verified done (fixture state file: seq+1 and the expected field). The state file mtime (CLOCK_REALTIME) is mapped to monotonic with a back-to-back pair; row field journal_before_done must be true (G2).
definitions_implemented.effect: Delta = mean over complete verified pairs of ln(T_candidate / T_champion); 95% percentile bootstrap CI (B=4000, seeded); one-sided p for H0 Delta >= 0 by null-shifted bootstrap
definitions_implemented.tau: max(0.02, exp(q) - 1), q = 97.5th percentile of |mean ln ratio| over AA batches of the planned size resampled from AA calibration pairs (champion in both arms)
definitions_implemented.n_pairs: ceil((z_.99 + z_.80)^2 (sigma/delta)^2), delta = ln(1 + tau); (z_.99 + z_.80)^2 = 10.04 (the plan's 10); floor --min-pairs (default 10)
definitions_implemented.lord_pp: alpha 0.05, W0 0.025, gamma_j = 0.0722 log(max(j,2)) / (j exp(sqrt(log j))); state = ordered p-values in results.jsonl; an index is consumed only when G5 is evaluated
gate_order: G7 mechanism share >= 0.7 and |Delta_off - Delta_on| <= ln(1+tau)
G8 soak >= 300 (1000 if focus_guard.rs or targeted.rs changed), zero failures
GS spot checks: equal verified counts, upper CI of Delta <= ln(1+tau)
definitions_implemented.verdicts: KEEP (all pass), REJECT (first failing gate), INCONCLUSIVE (G5 had fewer pairs than pre-registered; no LORD++ index consumed)

atspi_across_namespace.session_pidns_mode: WORKS: list_windows found the task window; get_window_state element_count 9, not degraded, not truncated; background element click returned route 'accessibility' and the fixture's own state file flipped (seq 1->2, agreed False->True)

atspi_across_namespace.exact_gap: Not an AT-SPI transport problem: the Driver resolves the target app through /proc/<pid>. tools/impl_.rs:561 keeps only windows whose pid is live in the Driver's own /proc (proc_fs::is_process_live); it also reads process start times and /proc/<pid>/maps|exe for toolkit detection. Under --unshare-pid the fixture's pid (from _NET_WM_PID, from AT-SPI peer credentials, and passed by the caller) does not exist in the sandbox's /proc. A child pid namespace holding the fixture would not fix it either, because the AT-SPI bus reports peer pids in its own namespace.
atspi_across_namespace.fallback_used: share the private SESSION's pid namespace (session-pidns.sh), never the host's. Weaker than a per-trial pid namespace: the Driver can list session processes (Xvfb, buses, openbox/picom, fixture, caller) and read their world-readable /proc files (cmdline: paths only), and could signal them (same uid); it cannot read their environ or reach their mount view through /proc/<pid>/root (denied from its child user namespace, probed). Mitigation: scanner rule 'signals' plus 'unsafe_or_asm'. An earlier probe with the HOST pid namespace showed 728 visible processes (also root/environ denied); that mode was dropped.

observations_for_orchestrator: hostless masks /tmp/.X11-unix and /run/user/<uid> but does not unshare the network namespace, and /proc/net/unix lists abstract X sockets in the host namespace (@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0, X2, X99, X100). A process under hostless that set DISPLAY=:0 could therefore reach whichever server owns @/tmp/.X11-unix/X0 through the abstract socket. Not tested by connecting (that could touch the host). The per-trial Driver sandbox here closes it with --unshare-net; the GTK fixture and caller only use the private session DISPLAY. Consider --unshare-net (or a private netns) in hostless.
The private session's dbus activates gvfs, whose fuse mount fails ('fusermount3: mount failed: Operation not permitted'); harmless, same in every session.
